??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Dagny. Dagny Roe. Night watch. Everyone calls me Two-Lamps, which is fair, because look: two lamps. I am awake. I am mostly awake. What can I do for you?
    - The little ones by the stackyards are young gloomeyes. I say it to them now: hello, young gloomeyes. They still do not answer. But the far ones, by the old walls, I still do not know.
    - You stood the watch with me! Nobody stands the watch with me. Knox does, a bit, but he carves, so it is more like standing the watch with a woodpile.
    - Brindle chalked your count in the good chalk. I saw. The prints are still there in the mornings, but now I know whose they are, and they are smaller in my head.
    - Every lantern on the outer wall is lit. I can see them from the gate, all along, like a necklace. I used to count the dark gaps. Now I count lights. It is a much nicer number.
    - Ask me anything. Please. It is a long night.
        - *Choice:* Why two lamps?
        - *Choice:* What do you see out there?
        - *Choice:* You and Patch?
        - *Choice:* Nothing. Goodbye.
    - My first month on the gate, late autumn, wet, my lamp went out. Just went. And there was something on the road. Moving. I stood there in the pitch black for a whole minute with my heart going like a drum.
    - It was a goat. A lost goat. I have never forgiven it. The next night I brought two lamps, and I have carried two ever since. My family renders lamp oil in Bain Harbour; I know how to keep a flame. I just like to keep two.
    - Eyes. Pairs of them, low down in the brush beyond the road, catching the lamplight and holding still. More this year than last. Some nights I can hear them breathing. So I step up to the edge of the light and talk at them. Because what else is there to do?
    - Gloomeyes. Lizards with lamps for eyes. Knowing makes it better and worse. Better, because they are only lizards. Worse, because there are so many of them.
    - Still eyes. Always eyes. But the touched ones, the ones that do not blink, there are fewer. I can tell. I still talk at them. It is a habit now. I think they would miss it.
    - Patch is my friend. On bad nights I bring the bitten ones to her door, and she scolds them while she bandages them, and then she scolds me for standing too near the road, and then she makes me a drink.
    - It is willow bark and something else she will not name, and it tastes like a boot, and it is the only reason I make it to dawn. After the last patient I walk her home with both lamps. She says it is unnecessary. She has never once said no.
    - Bye! Come back before dark. Or after. Either. Both lamps will be lit.
